thread:
maya: Heads up — observed a spike in cross-region traffic for EU users hitting us-east-1 yesterday (~1.2% of requests). Digging into routing rules.

derek: ah — likely the current geo-affinity TTL is too low. We're expiring the sticky header after 30s right now.

maya: yeah. proposal: increase affinity TTL to 5m for session-based routes and add latency ejection threshold so we only failover when p95 > 350ms for 3 consecutive probes.

sam: +1. can we also prefer zone-local within region before hitting cross-region? example: prefer zone A, then zone B in same region, then fallback region.

jessie: UI question — how will this look in Console rollouts? Should be a single "Regional affinity" toggle with advanced settings: TTL, latency threshold, fallback region order. We should surface expected cost impact.

maya: draft config we'd apply:
```
route {
  affinity_ttl: 300s
  latency_ejection: {p95_ms:350, probes:3}
  fallback_order: [local-zone, local-region, configured-fallback-region]
  header_override: "X-Region-Force"
}
```

derek: love it. one ask: make header override opt-in and scoped to orgs with Dedicated/Private plans. Otherwise public hosted customers might accidentally pin.

routing-bot: Probe results: eu-west-1 p95=220ms, eu-west-2 p95=210ms, us-east-1 p95=480ms — last check 2m ago.

sam: Also add telemetry: metric regional_affinity_hits, regional_ejections, header_pins_count. Add a per-route chart in Console.

jessie: UX: add a small yellow warning when enabling header_override: "Header pins can route traffic to a specific region — use with caution (billing & compliance implications)".

maya: I'll open a PR with config change + dashboard tiles. tagging @derek @jessie for review. :thumbsup:

derek: on it, will review today.

sam: i can add the telemetry queries to the dashboard after PR merges.
